summary: Accumulate from the final array element toward the first.
documentation: reduceRight passes the accumulator and each element to a callback in descending index order. Supplying an initial accumulator makes the empty-array result explicit. This is useful when each outer layer must wrap a result already built from the layers to its right.
inputs: An object with layers (a list of names) and leaf (a string).
returns: A nested object chain with each layer as {name, child}, ending in the leaf string.
caution: Without an initial value an empty array throws and the last element becomes the accumulator. The nesting direction matters: reducing left to right would make the last name the outermost layer.
scenarios: Build nested breadcrumb data from an ordered path.
Wrap a text node in successive layout descriptors for a preview.
Construct a nested configuration tree from outer-to-inner names.
title: Build an outer-to-inner chain
problem: Return layers as nested {name, child} objects in their original outer-to-inner order, with leaf as the innermost child. For no layers return leaf unchanged. Keep duplicate and empty names.
hint: Start with value.leaf and wrap the accumulator as you visit layers from right to left.
goal: Use Array.reduceRight() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
